title: OpenAMI Village Meter — Northbound MQTT Profile

includes: Normalized VMRS register payloads from edge gateway to operator HES
MQTT topic layout and JSON envelope
Correlation hooks to IETF Session Initiation Protocol (SIP, RFC 3261) dialogs for control-plane admission (optional Phase 3)
excludes: Full DLMS/COSEM object model on the wire
Normative SIP message syntax — use RFC 3261 / related IETF SIP specs

sip.name: Session Initiation Protocol
sip.standard: IETF RFC 3261 (SIP) and related RFCs (e.g. dialog, identity, TLS transport)
sip.roleInOpenAMI: Control-plane session setup — INVITE / ACK / BYE (and related methods) establish and tear down authenticated dialogs among gateways, policy servers, and market participants. MQTT carries VMRS telemetry and actuator commands; it does not replace SIP signaling.
openAMIUse: Admit a feeder or tenant into a DER / settlement / disconnect-authorized dialog before privileged commands
Bind MQTT telemetry and command topics to an active SIP dialog via Call-ID (and dialog tags when needed)
End authorization cleanly with BYE so orphaned disconnect or trade rights do not linger

mqttCorrelation.mapsTo: SIP Call-ID header of the controlling dialog
mqttCorrelation.commandGate: When a Phase 3 SIP dialog is in force, relay / disconnect / reconnect / settlement commands SHOULD bind to that dialog; Phase 1–2 prepaid and OpenAMI telemetry MUST NOT require SIP. Telemetry MAY omit sipCallId when no dialog is in force

sip.transports: SIP over UDP/TCP/TLS or SIP over WebSocket — operator choice; not carried inside the MQTT JSON envelope
sip.note: OpenAMI does not redefine SIP. This profile only states how northbound MQTT correlates to IETF SIP dialogs for village / mini-grid control. ISV roadmap: optional Phase 3 (grid connectivity) — not required for Phase 1 prepaid or Phase 2 OpenAMI MQTT telemetry. Contact Tech Comm (Glenn Algie / NESL Street-EMS track) for reference dialog flows.
